attempts.label: DANDI:000019
attempts.paper_title: Functional organization of human sensorimotor cortex for speech articulation
attempts.entry_title: Speech articulation in human sensorimotor cortex (Bouchard et al. 2013)
attempts.summary: No central finding was cleanly confirmed in this data. The dorsal-to-ventral layout of the articulators could not be tested, because the dataset lacks electrode positions relative to the central sulcus and Sylvian fissure. The staggered timing of articulator activity and the early peak of consonant separability did not reproduce. The state-space clustering results and the count of about 30 active electrodes stayed undecided, since the paper does not fix the baseline, z-scoring or syllable set. Mixed single-electrode tuning held, but under a test that barely discriminates. It needs to be written there.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Bouchard, Mesgarani, Johnson and Chang (2013) on dandiset 000019, which holds raw ECoG and syllable annotations of subjects reading consonant-vowel syllables. High gamma is computed from the raw voltage. It tests the active electrodes, the articulator timing, the mixed tuning of electrodes and the cortical state-space analyses. The spatial maps cannot be tested, as the dandiset gives no electrode positions relative to the central sulcus and Sylvian fissure.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Bouchard et al. (2013) from dandiset 000019

outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds four subjects (EC2, EC9, GP31, GP33); EC2, GP31 and GP33 are taken to be the paper's EC2, EC31 and EC33, and EC9 is not in the paper. The rate is 3051.76 Hz. The three subjects have 57, 55 and 57 CVs (169, paper 168), each with 19 consonants, and 2 to 107 renditions per CV (EC2 /thi/ 10, GP31 /thi/ 2, 33 GP31 CVs above 100); leaving out CVs below 15 renditions gives 56 + 54 + 57 = 167. The audio was removed. EC2 and GP31 have negative x coordinates (left hemisphere if x is the usual axis); GP33 has no coordinates, so the right hemisphere of EC33 cannot be checked. The answer of 2026-10-22 on CVs with fewer than 15 renditions leaves this claim as it was; the paper's 168 CVs fit neither reading, and the outcome is unchanged. No field in the files links GP31 and GP33 to EC31 and EC33; the subject fields hold only species and id, and the session descriptions name only the block. The electrode group of EC2 and GP31 is named `L256Grid electrodes` in every file, which fits a left hemisphere; that of GP33 is `auto_group`, with location `location`. In EC2 and GP31, 18 consonants have all three vowels with 15 or more renditions each, and in GP33 19, so GP31 fits the paper's subject with 18 consonants and 54 CVs.
deviations: The correspondence of GP31 and GP33 to the paper's EC31 and EC33 is an assumption; no metadata links them.

outcomes.notes: Mean active vSMC electrodes per subject. With every CV, 24.3 with the pre-utterance baseline (EC2 15, GP31 49, GP33 9), 21.3 with the whole block and 34.0 with the rest period; none is within 27 to 33, so this CV reading gives not reproduced. With only CVs of 15 or more renditions, 10.7, 7.0 and 27.0 (rest; EC2 29, GP31 31, GP33 21), so one baseline is within tolerance, at its lower edge, and this reading gives partially reproduced. Both readings of the change give the same counts. The count depends strongly on the threshold (41.7 at 1.5, 11.7 at 2.5, pre baseline, every CV). What the answers changed. The rest period, a variant in the first run, is now baseline reading (c) of the claims file, and the CV set is now a reading of the claims file whose two readings give different outcomes. The first run recorded not reproduced; the outcome is now blocked as methods_underspecified. Measured is the first reading (pre, every CV). The CV split comes from one syllable. Every GP31 electrode active with every CV but not with the 15+ CVs is above 2 for /thi/, which GP31 has 2 renditions of (40 electrodes under pre, 43 under whole, 20 under rest); in EC2 one electrode is active through /thi/ (10 renditions). A variant that leaves out the 162 trials overlapping intervals marked as ECoG artifacts, not a reading of the claims file, gives means of 22.7, 21.0 and 26.0 with every CV and 8.0, 6.7 and 15.0 with the 15+ CVs, none within 27 to 33; GP31's count under rest with the 15+ CVs falls from 31 to 2, so the one reading within tolerance rests on trials the files mark as artifacts.
deviations: High gamma computed from the raw ECoG with a filter bank whose widths the paper does not give (standard choice); bad channels from the dataset's flags.
vSMC taken as the electrodes labelled precentral or postcentral, good in every block (268 over the three subjects, paper 266); no label marks the guenon.

outcomes.notes: No subject, numbering from 1 or from 0, puts all six named electrodes on vSMC. The most is 5 of 6, in EC2 counted from 0, where e129 is labelled middle temporal; GP31 has at most 4 and GP33 at most 3. The criterion blocks the claim in that case. The dataset does not say how the paper numbered electrodes, and gives no distance from the Sylvian fissure for the order part. For information, in EC2 counted from 1 (3 of 6 on vSMC), five of the six named electrodes prefer their syllable under both measures and all three baselines; counted from 0, two or three do. The answer of 2026-10-22 to the question on positions says the paper measures them on each subject's MRI reconstruction and gives no way to derive them from grid geometry, unlabelled coordinates or atlas labels, so the block stands.

Under all 96 readings (3 baselines, 2 CV sets, 8 timing readings for T_A, 2 p-value readings) no GLM electrode with a positive lips weight has z above 2 for /ju/ at +250 ms and below 2 for /ja/ and /ji/ in any subject. With the rest baseline some lips-positive electrodes exceed 2 for /ju/ (13 of 96 readings, largest 3.54), but at each of them /ja/ or /ji/ is above 2 as well; under the pre and whole baselines the largest /ju/ value is below 2. The fricative and manner contrasts are not judged, as the claims file says. What the answers changed. The rest baseline and the CV set are now readings of the claims file; the 32 rest readings added give the same outcome, not reproduced, as in the first run. Without the GLM selection, among all vSMC electrodes, one EC2 electrode under rest (both CV sets) has /ju/ above 2 and /ja/ and /ji/ below 2; under pre and whole no vSMC electrode in any subject reaches 2 for /ju/ (largest 1.19), so there the result does not come from the selection.
deviations: The lips weights come from the GLM of fig2a-lips-dorsal, which is blocked for its spatial judgement only; the weights and electrode selection need no positions and are computed, so this claim is tested.

outcomes.notes: The claim judges where the lips and tongue weights lie as dorsal-ventral distance from the Sylvian fissure. The dandiset gives no electrode position relative to the Sylvian fissure or the central sulcus. EC2 and GP31 have x, y, z coordinates with no unit or frame; GP33 has none. The GLM electrodes and weights are computed (they need no positions) and used by fig1f-h, suppfig6 and suppfig9. For information only, under the first reading the median z coordinate of the top 10% of lips weights is above that of the tongue weights in EC2 (36.6 against 15.6); GP31 has no tongue window in that reading, so it gives no comparison. The answer of 2026-10-22 to the question on positions says the paper measures them on each subject's MRI reconstruction and gives no way to derive them from grid geometry, unlabelled coordinates or atlas labels, so the block stands.

Needs positions relative to the central sulcus and Sylvian fissure in all three subjects (see fig2a-lips-dorsal). The answer of 2026-10-22 to the question on positions says the paper measures them on each subject's MRI reconstruction and gives no way to derive them from grid geometry, unlabelled coordinates or atlas labels, so the block stands.

Needs the smoothed maps in the plane of distances from the central sulcus and Sylvian fissure (see fig2a-lips-dorsal). The answer of 2026-10-22 to the question on positions says the paper measures them on each subject's MRI reconstruction and gives no way to derive them from grid geometry, unlabelled coordinates or atlas labels, so the block stands.

Needs maps in a common frame across subjects, from distances to the central sulcus and Sylvian fissure (see fig2a-lips-dorsal); GP33 has no coordinates at all. The answer of 2026-10-22 to the question on positions says the paper measures them on each subject's MRI reconstruction and gives no way to derive them from grid geometry, unlabelled coordinates or atlas labels, so the block stands.

Needs the maps of suppfig3b-spatial-clustering (see fig2a-lips-dorsal). The answer of 2026-10-22 to the question on positions says the paper measures them on each subject's MRI reconstruction and gives no way to derive them from grid geometry, unlabelled coordinates or atlas labels, so the block stands.

Needs Euclidean distances in mm between electrodes in the paper's plane (see fig2a-lips-dorsal). The EC2 and GP31 coordinates have no stated unit or frame, and GP33 has none. The answer of 2026-10-22 to the question on positions says the paper measures them on each subject's MRI reconstruction and gives no way to derive them from grid geometry, unlabelled coordinates or atlas labels, so the block stands.

Under all 96 readings, each group of GLM electrodes (grouped by largest weight) has its preferred articulator with the largest mean share of positive weight (lips 63 to 79%, tongue 48 to 96%, larynx 49 to 84%, jaw 69 to 84%) and non-zero shares of the others; in one reading no electrode prefers the tongue. The GLM electrodes number 49 to 117 over the three subjects. In the readings where a subject has no window T_A for an articulator, its weights there are missing. What the answers changed. The rest baseline and the CV set are now readings of the claims file; the 32 rest readings added hold as well, and the outcome is reproduced, as in the first run. The criterion barely discriminates. On weights permuted across each subject's electrodes, which removes any tuning of single electrodes, the same test holds in 94 of 96 readings, because grouping by the largest weight puts the preferred articulator first almost by construction. The outcome follows the criterion; a clear preferred articulator beyond what the grouping gives is not shown by it.
deviations: Uses the GLM weights of fig2a-lips-dorsal, which is blocked for its spatial judgement only.

outcomes.notes: Under all 96 readings (3 baselines, 2 CV sets, threshold per subject or pooled and over all articulators or per articulator, onset at threshold or half peak, ANOVA on onset or peak) none of the three order conditions holds. Mean lips onsets are -270 to -54 ms, but tongue onsets are -26 to +290 ms, so lips and tongue both precede the substitute acoustic onset (-110 ms, CV range -257 to -11 ms) in no reading; jaw onsets are -270 to -116 ms, as early as the lips; high-tongue peaks are 276 to 325 ms. Against t = 0, shown beside it as the criterion now asks, lips and tongue both begin before 0 ms in 2 of 96 readings and the outcome is the same. The ANOVA has F = 9.4 to 39.2 with p below 1e-10 in 76 of 96 readings. Electrodes 162 to 226 (paper 211). Measured values are from the first reading (175 electrodes; mean of back and high tongue peaks, 235 and 305 ms). What the answers changed. The criterion now allows the hand-marked syllable start as the acoustic onset, as a deviation, which the first run had used while asking; the rest baseline and the CV set are now readings. The outcome is not reproduced, as in the first run. Tongue electrodes number 2 to 7 under the readings with one threshold for all six articulators (2 to 45 over all readings), so those tongue onsets rest on few electrodes. A variant that leaves out the trials overlapping intervals marked as ECoG artifacts gives the same outcome (one condition holds in 4 of 96 readings, none in the others; lips onsets -338 to -125 ms, tongue -6 to 289 ms).
deviations: The acoustic onset is the hand-marked syllable start of the trial table, averaged per CV, as the audio is not in the dandiset; the criterion allows this substitute since the answer of 2026-10-22. The outcome against t = 0 is the same.

outcomes.notes: Needs electrodes within 10 mm anterior and posterior of the central sulcus and the guenon's boundary; the dandiset gives no distances to the central sulcus and no guenon label. The answer of 2026-10-22 to the question on positions says the paper measures them on each subject's MRI reconstruction and gives no way to derive them from grid geometry, unlabelled coordinates or atlas labels, so the block stands.

With row z-scoring, nine PCs explain a mean of 0.60 to 0.66 over subjects, within 0.54 to 0.66 in 11 of 12 baseline, CV set and window readings (rest, every CV, -375 to 620 ms gives 0.661). With time z-scoring, 0.49 to 0.56, within under the rest baseline (4 readings) and once under the whole block, outside in the other 7. The readings give different outcomes (16 within, 8 not). The variance explained does not depend on the input projected. No sharp change at the ninth eigenvalue is seen; not judged. Measured is the first reading (pre, row, every CV, epoch). What the answers changed. The paper fixes neither z-scoring nor the CV set, which the claims file now names as readings, and the rest period is now a baseline reading; the outcome stays blocked as methods_underspecified, as in the first run. The z-scoring decides most of the split (row 11 of 12 within, time 5 of 12); the CV set and the window do not change the count (8 of 12 within each).

Under 23 of the 24 readings (3 baselines, 2 z-scorings, 2 projections, 2 CV sets) k = 3 does not have the highest mean silhouette (not reproduced). Under one, rest baseline, time z-scoring, projection (i) and every CV, k = 3 is highest by a small margin (0.333 against 0.329 for k = 2 and 0.241 for k = 4), with values outside tolerance (partially reproduced). k = 3 gives 0.19 to 0.36 against the paper's 0.47. GP31's k = 2 silhouette is 0.35 to 0.80 with every CV and 0.24 to 0.68 with CVs of 15 or more renditions. Measured values are the first reading (pre, row, projection i, every CV) for k = 3, 2 and 4. What the answers changed. The rest baseline and projection (ii) are now readings, and one of the readings added gives partially reproduced, so the readings differ. The first run recorded not reproduced; the outcome is now blocked as methods_underspecified. Over the 24 readings k = 2 has the highest mean silhouette in 20, k = 4 in 3 and k = 3 in 1.

Clusters match the major articulators beyond chance in every reading (consonant p from 9e-23 to 3e-13). Observed consonant medians 0.633 to 0.909 with labels (a) and 0.595 to 0.800 with labels (b) (paper 0.50 +- 0.05), vowel medians 0.41 to 0.70 (paper 0.65 +- 0.065), nulls 0.336 to 0.412 for consonants and 0.343 to 0.430 for vowels (paper 0.32 and 0.37). Of the 48 readings (24 by two label readings) 38 give partially reproduced. In five readings, all with projection (i) (row with 15+ CVs under each baseline, rest with row and every CV, rest with time and 15+ CVs), the vowel test gives p from 3e-10 to 5e-07, above 1e-10, and not reproduced under both label readings. Projection (ii) gives partially reproduced in all 24 of its readings. Each label reading is judged with its own consonant test and the vowel test. Measured is the first reading (pre, row, projection i, every CV, labels a). What the answers changed. The answers left z-scoring and the CV set open and added the rest baseline and projection (ii) as readings; projection (ii) gives partially reproduced in every reading, and the outcome stays blocked as methods_underspecified, as in the first run.

Both splits hold together in at most one subject, EC2 (14 of 24 readings), so no reading gives reproduced; 28 of the 48 readings (with the two label readings) give partially reproduced and 20 not reproduced. Under time z-scoring with projection (i) no subject meets both. The vowel split never holds in GP31. The purity rule of two thirds is the claims file's own. What the answers changed. The rest baseline and projection (ii) are now readings, and z-scoring and the CV set stay open; the outcome stays blocked as methods_underspecified, as in the first run. Projection (ii) gives partially reproduced in 20 of 24 readings and projection (i) in 8 of 24; the CV set and the label reading do not change the counts (14 of 24 each).

Early window, location over degree over vowel with p < 1e-10 under every Euclidean reading (n = 297) except two (rest, projection i, 15+ CVs, location over degree p = 3e-05 and 3e-04). Late window, the vowel features correlate more than both other sets with p < 1e-10 in 10 of 24 readings (reproduced), every 15+ reading with projection (ii) among them; the other 14 give partially reproduced, mostly with every CV, where location correlates as much as or more than the vowel features. Hamming distances are a variant and are not judged. What the answers changed. The rest baseline and projection (ii) are now readings, and z-scoring and the CV set stay open; the readings still give reproduced and partially reproduced, and the outcome stays blocked as methods_underspecified, as in the first run. Projection (ii) gives 8 of the 10 reproduced readings, and the 15+ CVs 8 of 10.

Under all 120 readings (24 baseline, z-scoring, projection and CV readings by five cluster readings) the peaks are not both within tolerance. With phonetic groups the consonant peak is at -155 to +15 ms (paper -200) and the vowel peak at 155 to 235 ms; with k-means at each time one curve serves both, peaking between -170 and 375 ms. Consonant onsets (reading a) are -375 to -180 ms, vowel onsets 55 to 105 ms. Measured is the first reading (pre, row, projection i, every CV, groups a; onset reading a). What the answers changed. The rest baseline and projection (ii) are now readings; the readings added give the same outcome, not reproduced, as in the first run. After the first verification the bootstrap no longer pairs a token with its own copies, which changes only the s.e. of onset reading (a) (first reading's vowel onset 100 to 105 ms); every reading factor still gives not reproduced in all its readings.
deviations: The onset reading (a) takes the curve's value at -500 ms as its pre-epoch level, the earliest time of the epoch. The claims file says "pre-epoch level" without a time; this is the attempt's choice, and it decides only the onset, not the peaks on which the outcome rests.

outcomes.notes: With phonetic-group clusters and the matching feature set (location for consonants, vowel for vowels), the six R2 lie within 0.38 to 1 with p < 1e-10 in 80 of 96 readings, are positive and significant with some below 0.38 in 15, and fail in 1 (R2 0.14 to 0.99). With the mean of the three feature sets, or with k-means clusters, the coupling fails in every reading. The claims file's own readings give different outcomes. What the answers changed. The rest baseline and projection (ii) are now readings; the outcome stays blocked as methods_underspecified, as in the first run. Two readings of the claims file decide the split, that of R and that of the clusters. With the mean of three feature sets all 120 readings fail, and with k-means clusters all 48 fail, the 24 with the matching feature set among them. Every level of the baseline, z-scoring, projection and CV set has both reproduced and not reproduced readings, so the split does not come from these details.

With row z-scoring, and with time z-scoring and projection (ii), consonant-vowel distances exceed consonant-consonant ones, which exceed vowel-vowel ones, with corrected p < 1e-10; with time z-scoring and projection (i) the consonant-vowel distances are shorter than the consonant-consonant ones in every baseline and CV set. The pairs number 4677 (every CV) or 4567 (15+ CVs), not 4623, so no reading meets the criterion as written. The criterion defines only reproduced; a reading where all orderings hold and only the pair count differs is counted as partially reproduced (36 of 48), by the protocol's general definition of an effect that holds in part, and one where an ordering fails as not reproduced (12, all with time z-scoring and projection (i)). Read strictly, every reading is not reproduced; the outcome is kept blocked because the pair count is fixed by the dataset's syllables (data-composition), while whether the orderings hold depends on readings the paper does not fix. What the answers changed. The paper fixes neither z-scoring nor the CV set, and projection (ii), added as a reading, gives the orderings under both z-scorings; the outcome stays blocked as methods_underspecified, as in the first run.

Under all 288 readings the condition fails in all three PCs; tongue weights are not larger than lips weights. In the reading printed in full (268 vSMC electrodes, pre, every CV) lips minus tongue has a median paired difference of +0.03 in log10 (corrected p = 1), and jaw and larynx differ (corrected p = 5e-11). By Methods Eq. 6 the PC term cancels in paired comparisons of one electrode's articulators, so the three PCs give the same tests. What the answers changed. The rest baseline is now a reading (96 readings added); the input projected does not enter this test. The outcome is not reproduced, as in the first run. Electrodes without a window T_A for an articulator are dropped, none in 168 readings, up to 83 in the others (GP31 lacks a tongue window in some timing readings), leaving 32 to 268 electrodes; every reading fails either way.
deviations: Uses the GLM weights of fig2a-lips-dorsal, which is blocked for its spatial judgement only.

findings.statement: No electrode has a position relative to the central sulcus or the Sylvian fissure, the frame of the paper's spatial analyses. EC2 and GP31 have x, y, z coordinates with no unit or coordinate frame described; GP33 and EC9 have none. No electrode is labelled as on the guenon. Seven spatial findings of the paper cannot be tested.

The microphone recordings were removed (dandiset description), so the acoustic onset, peak and offset of each syllable used by the paper cannot be computed; only hand-marked start, C-V transition and stop times are given.

Subjects GP31 and GP33 do not carry the paper's names (EC31, EC33), and nothing links them. GP31's coordinates fit a left hemisphere, as the paper's EC31; GP33 has no coordinates, so the right hemisphere of EC33 cannot be checked. The subject fields hold only species and id. The electrode group of EC2 and GP31 is `L256Grid electrodes`; that of GP33 is `auto_group`, with location `location`, so no field gives GP33's hemisphere.
The dandiset holds a fourth subject, EC9 (7 blocks, 1653 trials), that is not in the paper. It has extra syllables (/ch/, /dh/, /j/, /sk/), labels on 79 of 256 electrodes and no coordinates.

Renditions per syllable range from 2 to 107 (GP31 /thi/ 2, EC2 /thi/ 10, GP31 up to 107) against the paper's 15 to 100, and GP31 lacks /tha/ and /thu/. The three subjects have 169 distinct syllables against the paper's 168 (57 + 57 + 54). The dandiset does not say which trials or syllables the paper used.

The raw ElectricalSeries gives unit volt with a conversion factor of 0.001, but the stored values have an SD of a few 1e-5, which is a usual ECoG amplitude if read as volts and tens of nanovolts with the factor; the data are consistent with values already in volts.
Two syllable labels are misspelt (`she` for `shee` in EC2 and EC9, `ha` for `haa` in GP33 and EC9). Electrode ids start at 0 in EC2 and GP31 and at 1 in GP33 and EC9.

The archive summary counts four subjects and 31 files; bad-channel flags differ between blocks of one subject (EC2 has none in two blocks and up to 10 in others), and 162 of 9370 analysed trials overlap intervals marked as ECoG artifacts (38 in GP31 block 63, whose rest period has a high-gamma SD of 0.3 times the block's). One file (EC2 block 1) holds a power spectrum of the 256 channels in a processing module; no other file has one.
